column1: # Artifacts for scripts/validate-pades-profile.sh, which asks European Commission DSS what
# PAdES baseline profile each committed artifact actually reaches. Separate from manifest.tsv
# on purpose: that one records pyHanko's verdicts, and the two tools do not agree on every
# artifact (see sealed-b-t-untrusted-tsa.pdf below). Findings: docs/stage0/pades-profile.md.
# The artifacts themselves are regenerated by the pyHanko job, not this one:
#   ESIGN_WRITE_VALIDATION_FIXTURES=1 php artisan test --filter=ValidationFixturesTest
# This check reads the committed bytes exactly as they are, which is what
# docs/stage0/sealing.md promised a later DSS pass would do.
# Columns: file<TAB>trust<TAB>level<TAB>conclusion<TAB>timestamps<TAB>note
#   trust        which anchor DSS is given, and the only one it is given:
#                  fixture-only          tests/Fixtures/crypto/root.test.crt
#                  rotation-target-only  tests/Fixtures/crypto/root-b.test.crt
#                A file may appear more than once under different trust modes. That is how the
#                seal-key rotation rows show the two anchors actually discriminate, rather than
#                a validator that trusts everything. There is no fixture-plus-system mode here:
#                this check is never given an OS trust store, so it claims nothing about a
#                public timestamp authority.
#   level        the SignatureLevel DSS reports, or '-' when there is no single signature to
#                report one for. This is DSS's structural profile verdict and it is the reason
#                this check exists: a signature that were merely a valid PKCS#7 rather than a
#                conformant baseline signature would read PKCS7_B or PDF_NOT_ETSI here.
#   conclusion   the AdES conclusion, INDICATION or INDICATION/SUB_INDICATION exactly, or
#                'unreadable' when DSS refuses to open the file at all, or 'no-signature'.
#                Matched exactly, so a change in what DSS concludes is a failure, not a shrug.
#   timestamps   'none', or '<count>:<conclusion>[,<conclusion>...]' for the signature
#                timestamps. Reported separately because DSS can call a signature TOTAL_PASSED
#                at BASELINE_T while the timestamp's own certificate chain is untrusted.
# No OS store, no EU trusted list, no online CRL or OCSP fetch, ever. That is why both B-T
# artifacts report their timestamp as NO_CERTIFICATE_CHAIN_FOUND — DigiCert's root is not an
# input here. TSA trust is pyHanko's half of the evidence (manifest.tsv, fixture-plus-system
# mode), not this one's.
sealed-b-b.pdf
column6: The B-B claim in docs/stage0/sealing.md, now backed by a profile verdict rather than a soundness check.

column1: sealed-b-t.pdf
column6: B-T structurally. The timestamp is from DigiCert and is sound; its chain is untrusted here only because this run is given the fixture root alone.

column1: sealed-b-t-untrusted-tsa.pdf
column6: DIVERGENCE, deliberate: pyHanko judges this artifact INVALID on TSA trust, DSS calls the signature TOTAL_PASSED because an untrusted signature timestamp does not sink a B-T conclusion — it only fails to contribute a trusted POE. Both verdicts are correct about different questions; neither is tuned to agree.

column1: finalized-executed.pdf
column6: The executed agreement from staged finalization, sealed at B-B. Same profile verdict as the bare B-B artifact.

column1: rotation-retired-key.pdf
column6: Sealed under the RETIRED key (fixture-seal-2026-a), under the retired certificate's own anchor. A rotation does not change what profile the old key's artifacts satisfy, and it does not invalidate them.

column1: rotation-active-key.pdf
column6: Sealed under the ACTIVE key after rotation (fixture-seal-2026-b), under the new certificate's anchor. The new key produces the same baseline profile as the old one.

column1: rotation-retired-key.pdf
column6: The retired artifact under the NEW key's anchor. Still structurally BASELINE_B — the profile is a property of the signature, not of who trusts it — but no path to an anchor. The pair of anchors discriminates, so the TOTAL_PASSED rows above are about the right certificate.

column1: rotation-active-key.pdf
column6: The active artifact under the RETIRED key's anchor: the complement of the row above.

column1: negative-modified-content.pdf
column6: Page geometry changed inside the signed byte range. The level still reads BASELINE_B because the structure is untouched; the level is a statement about form, never a verdict.

column1: negative-forged-cms.pdf
column6: The CMS of another sealed document spliced into /Contents.

column1: negative-byte-range-overclaim.pdf
column6: /ByteRange claims past the end of a file that still parses. DSS reports it as a format failure, adding "The /ByteRange dictionary is not consistent!".

column1: negative-incremental-update.pdf
column6: An unexpected revision appended, redefining the page object. This is TOTAL_FAILED only because tools/dss/validation-policy.xml raises DSS's UndefinedChanges constraint from WARN to FAIL; under DSS's stock policy the conclusion is identical to a clean artifact's. Recorded in docs/stage0/pades-profile.md, not hidden.

column1: negative-untrusted-signer.pdf
column6: Cryptographically sound but sealed outside the trusted root. INDETERMINATE, not TOTAL_FAILED: nothing about the signature is broken, there is simply no path to an anchor.

column1: negative-truncated.pdf
column6: Tail removed with the trailer. DSS never reaches the signature, so this row pins a refusal to parse and says nothing about the byte range; negative-byte-range-overclaim.pdf is what carries the coverage property.
